spec.cue: Hold still, as a jumping spider watches. Its big front eyes pick out what is sharp, and the side eyes catch anything that moves.

fov.note: the whole animal's field, with the side eyes near 360 degrees and the six smaller eyes near 300

cpd.note: typical principal eye acuity, measured in Phidippus johnsoni

gate.note: the app's choice; the side eyes answer to movement, so still things fade

sat.note: the app's choice; two colour classes give less than full colour

rows: The big front pair sees fine detail and colour in a narrow strip about 2 degrees wide and 21 high. The side eyes take in almost the whole circle around the animal and respond to movement.
The front eyes resolve about 3.8 cycles in each degree, a little under a quarter of a person's best. Portia, the best case, reaches about 12.5.
The front eyes carry two pigment classes, one for ultraviolet and one for green, so colour is seen in a reduced palette. The ultraviolet is drawn from the blue channel of the phone.
The front eyes sweep the scene side to side and twist, rather than staying still. The picture follows this scan, and stationary things fade as the side eyes see only movement.
The strength of the glow, the lingering of the picture, the sharpness falloff, the saturation and the timings of attention are the app's guesses. No record gives them.

claims.how: The whole animal is given as 360 degrees by one record and near 300 degrees for the six smaller eyes by another; 300 is set between them, graded g.
Phidippus johnsoni principal eye acuity is given as 0.13 degrees, which is 3.8 cycles per degree.
The front zone uses the same principal eye acuity of 3.8 cycles per degree.
The principal retina is about 2 degrees wide and 21 high in object space.
Horizontal sweeps are at least 2 degrees across with a period of 1.1 to 1.3 seconds.
Retinae turn 20 to 30 degrees each way, about 2 seconds to turn, and are held 2 to 5 seconds at each end.
Smooth tracking was tested below 10 degrees a second.
Peaks at 359 nm (UV) and 526 nm (green) are both given by Saitis barbipes.
The side eyes behave as though completely blind to stationary objects, so still things fade fully; the value 1 is the app's switch, graded i.
